title: Egress canary & rule-migration tooling for private VPC Terraform module
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Provide a safe, observable path to change security group and NACL egress policies in private VPC deployments via Terraform without application downtime. Deliver a reusable module extension and a lightweight migration runner that can perform canary applies, run health probes, verify private DNS and egress behavior, and automatically roll back when checks fail.

Background: Customers in Private mode frequently need to tighten egress controls or migrate rules as we introduce new subnet layouts and outbound proxies (egress gateways). Previous one-shot Terraform applies have caused transient outages when rule ordering or NACL priorities changed. This ticket implements tooling and patterns to make those migrations predictable and testable in production-like environments.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module adds an optional 'egress_migration' submodule and flagging mechanism to create canary rules alongside existing rules
A migration runner (serverless job or CI step) can apply canary changes in a controlled subset of subnets and produce machine-readable diffs
Health-check suite validates: outbound TCP/HTTP to configured endpoints, DNS resolution for private zones, and token-store/KV access patterns; failures prevent promotion
Rollback path documented and automated: if probes fail, runner reverts canary changes and opens an incident ticket template
Module design avoids resource replacement for primary SG/NACL resources; uses additive rule resources and idempotent naming to keep drift low
End-to-end demo performed in staging and runbook added to Confluence with checklist and common troubleshooting steps
implementation_notes: Module changes: introduce 'egress_migration' optional block that creates 'egress_canary' security group rules and NACL entries instead of mutating primary rule sets
Terraform pattern: prefer aws_security_group_rule and aws_network_acl_rule separate resources (stable addresses) rather than inlined lists to prevent full-resource replacement
Naming convention: {env}-{cluster}-egress-canary-{counter} with predictable tags to find canaries for promotion/cleanup

Migration runner: small Go/Node binary executed as a GitHub Actions job or Lambda; responsibilities: plan/apply for canary scope, run probe harness from a runner EC2 in target subnet, evaluate thresholds, promote or revert

Health probes: curl against public endpoints via egress gateway, DNS lookups for private zones using 'dig +short @<resolver> <name>', and a synthetic application-level request that validates request/response shape

Promotion strategy: once canary passes N consecutive checks (configurable, default 3), runner flips a 'promote=true' variable in module and re-applies to add rules to the primary scope; keep an audit tag on promoted rules
Rollback: runner stores plan output and state snapshots in S3 with KMS encryption for quick revert; if promotion validation fails, it triggers a revert apply using the prior snapshot
Observability: emit events to CloudWatch/Datadog (canary.start, canary.pass, canary.fail, promote.start, promote.complete) with run ids and diff summaries
Backward compatibility: module defaults to 'migration disabled' so existing stacks are unchanged until teams opt-in
Testing: unit TF tests using terratest for resource creation, and integration test harness in staging that exercises cross-AZ hitting private DNS records
progress_updates: 2025-08-12 Ava Chen: RFC drafted and shared in #infra-privnet. Proposed 'canary as first-class' pattern to avoid rule replacements.
2025-08-18 Diego Marquez: Prototype submodule created: modules/egress_migration with basic SG rule creation. Ran plan in sandbox and confirmed no replacement of existing security group resources.
2025-08-25 Diego Marquez: Implemented initial runner in GH Actions (infra/egress-migration-runner). Runner can apply canary rules scoped to tag 'canary-test-01' and store plan JSON to S3.

2025-08-29 QA: Health probe harness added (scripts/probes) that run DNS and HTTP checks from an instance in the private subnet. Discovered that private DNS needs conditional forwarding update; created follow-up ENG-13089.
2025-09-02 Diego Marquez: Added Datadog events for canary lifecycle and updated Confluence runbook draft. Preparing staging demo next week.
review_feedback: 2025-08-20 Raj Patel (Security): Prefer additive rules only; avoid changing rule ordering semantics in NACLs. Also requested KMS key usage for S3 snapshots — added requirement.
2025-08-26 Lina Ortiz (PM): Requested 'dry-run' mode be default in GH Actions for first 2 cycles and clear customer-facing messaging about maintenance windows.
2025-08-30 Marco Li (Platform): Suggested using a short-lived IAM role for the runner with least privilege and tagging enforcement for cleanup automation.
notes_for_followup: Coordinate with private DNS owners to add conditional forwarding for canary resolver IPs
Schedule staging demo with SRE and Security for sign-off before GA
Add feature flag in Console to opt clusters into automatic canary promotions (future work)
